metadata.title: Human-Centered Design Strategies for Sustainability and Livelihood in Gond Tribal Art of Madhya Pradesh
metadata.description:
Abstract: This research investigates how human-centered design strategies can enhance sustainability and livelihood within the traditional art practices of the Gond tribe in Madhya Pradesh. The study aims to answer how design-oriented approaches can support Gond artists in preserving cultural identity while achieving economic resilience within a changing socio-economic landscape. Using a qualitative methodology, the study integrates literature review, field observations, case studies, and interviews with artists, scholars, and institutional representatives. It also analyzes policy frameworks and NGO initiatives that influence the socio-economic conditions of tribal artisans. The findings focus on how Gond art operates as a cultural and economic system, where traditional motifs and visual narratives are adapted through new materials, technologies, and market strategies without losing their symbolic depth. Human-centered design thinking helps reinterpret indigenous knowledge into sustainable livelihood models that balance creativity and income generation.
Practical Implications: This study contributes to the discourse on sustainable tribal livelihoods by position-ing Gond art as a model for culturally grounded design innovation. It demonstrates how design strategies connected to community participation and empathy can foster resilience, self-reliance, and cultural continuity in indigenous creative economies.

metadata.title: The Universal Appeal of Rajasthani Block Prints: Design, Human-Centered Strategy and Ergonomic Design Interventions for Contemporary Applications
metadata.description:
Abstract: Rajasthani block printing is one of the finest traditional crafts of the textile world in India; it’s kind of famous for its very elaborate designs, organic shades, and that steady, careful craftsmanship. Over time, this art form has not only stayed local; it has also become an international design tradition, seen in fashion, home decor, everyday items, and sustainable textiles, and yeah, it has spread across many regions over centuries. Nowadays, Rajasthani block prints feel even more attractive to the international market because demand keeps rising for handcrafted, earth-friendly products. But there’s a flip side too: changing buyer preferences, globalization, and technological changes have created hurdles for artisans. So, some fresh innovative approaches are needed to keep traditional artisan skills alive while still meeting what the modern market expects. This research is trying to look into the universal appeal of Rajasthani block prints, but by combining that idea with human and ergonomic design interventions. Human-centred design is basically a design approach that wants to understand the needs, preferences, and lived experiences of the user, so the results can be visually pleasing, practical, and culturally respectful. Meanwhile, ergonomic interventions focus on improving comfort, usability, accessibility and also productivity, both for artisans themselves and for the end users.
Practical Implications: The study examines how these strategies can help product innovation, especially in maintaining the authenticity of traditional block-printing techniques. It also goes further into why sustainable materials matter, how inclusive design practices can work in real life, and how digital marketing along with global branding can expand market potential for Rajasthani block-printed products. Finally, the research points out possible opportunities for strengthening artisans’ livelihoods and increasing the competitiveness of Indian handicrafts internationally.

metadata.title: The Influence of Folk Art on Contemporary Artistic and Design Practices
metadata.description:
Abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of folk art and crafts on modern design practices. It will focus on how designers can find innovative ways to apply folk art aesthetic, design languages to evolve and integrate new design languages. The second aspect is how designers can take advantage of technology to achieve desired effects without disturbing the traditional values of the folk arts and crafts. Folk art is deeply rooted in the cultural essence of a region, profoundly influenced by its soil, nature, and geographical characteristics. The close connection between people and their environment is evident in their artistic expressions, where bold and straightforward forms reflect their intrinsic bond with nature. This connection is further exemplified in their vibrant use of colors, linear depictions, and decorative motifs that breathe life into their homes, attire, and everyday objects. The graphic qualities of folk art—its simplicity, charm, and directness—remain fascinating and captivating.
India boasts a rich and diverse tradition of folk art and craft. Each region’s artistic expressions mirror the country’s cultural diversity, shaped by the distinct geographical features of its provinces. Folk art and craft are inseparable from the daily lives of the people, intricately linked to their festivals, rituals, and seasonal changes, which are often tied to agricultural and religious practices. These art forms embody the rhythm of life, weaving together nature and human activity.
For artists and designers, this vibrant lifestyle and its associated art forms—such as dance, music, textiles, pottery, cane work, and geometric crafts—offer a wealth of inspiration. These folk traditions present unique opportunities for exploring functionality, aesthetics, and decoration. The simplification of forms and motifs, particularly of animals, birds, and flora, often serves as a creative foundation for modern interpretations.
This study delves into the inspirational impact of folk art on contemporary artists and illustrators, many of whom have formal training in modern or academic art. Despite their backgrounds, these creators often integrate elements of tribal and folk art into their work, blending these influences with their unique design sensibilities to produce innovative artistic expressions. By analyzing these works, this study uncovers how folk-art traditions resonate within modern creative practices and explores the artistic parameters that define this interaction.
In addition to artistic creations, designers and illustrators have found innovative ways to apply folk aesthetics in communication design. The influence of folk art is evident in advertising, publication design, environmental graphics, outdoor publicity, and editorial illustrations. These contemporary applications demonstrate the enduring relevance of folk aesthetics, as they resonate strongly with the cultural psyche, creating a sense of “Indian-ness” that connects with people across social strata and popular culture. The impact of folk art extends beyond individual creations, influencing the broader field of design education. By studying how artists and designers adapt folk aesthetics, we can identify key inspirational elements that inform modern teaching methodologies.
Practical Implications: Practical exercises based on these findings can be integrated into contemporary design education, fostering a deeper appreciation of folk traditions while equipping students with innovative tools for creative expression. The approach of this study encourages the continuation of folk art’s legacy, ensuring its relevance in modern artistic and design practices. The study not only highlights the cultural significance of these traditions but also offers a roadmap for their integration into the evolving landscape of art and design.

metadata.title: Lampang style Buddha at The Sainsbury Centre for Visual Arts, UEA, Norwich
metadata.description: Buddhism started with the Buddha. The word 'Buddha' is a title, which means 'one who is awake' — in the sense of having 'woken up to reality'. The Buddha was born as Siddhartha Gautama in Nepal around 2,500 years ago. He did not claim to be a god or a prophet. He was a human being who became Enlightened, understanding life in the deepest way possible.  Siddhartha was born into the royal family of a small kingdom on the Indian-Nepalese border. According to the traditional story he had a privileged upbringing, but was jolted out of his sheltered life on realising that life includes the harsh facts of old age, sickness, and death.  This prompted him to puzzle over the meaning of life. Eventually he felt impelled to leave his palace and follow the traditional Indian path of the wandering holy man, a seeker after Truth. He became very adept at meditation under various teachers, and then took up ascetic practices. This was based on the belief that one could free the spirit by denying the flesh. He practised austerities so determinedly that he almost starved to death.     This object is part of Scan The World. Scan the World is a non-profit initiative introduced by MyMiniFactory, through which we are creating a digital archive of fully 3D printable sculptures, artworks and landmarks from across the globe for the public to access for free. Scan the World is an open source, community effort, if you have interesting items around you and would like to contribute, email stw@myminifactory.com to find out how you can help.

metadata.title: Hillsong Church (Global)
metadata.description:
Pentecostal and charismatic evangelical Christian movement originally linked with the Assemblies of God Pentecostal denomination. It started in Australia in 1983 as Hills Christian Life Centre in the Sydney suburbs, led by pastor Brian and his wife Bobbie Houston. The Sydney church grew to become a megachurch and the movement expanded through Australia, and later to the UK, South Africa, Ukraine, Sweden and other countries, through planting new congregations. Hillsong churches are now in 30-35 countries on five continents, almost exclusively operating as single large congregations in urban environments. Attendance numbers at in-person services are dwarfed by its global presence and brand on social media and via its music, including Instagram (2.8 million followers in 2026) and YouTube (its Hillsong United band has 5.6 million subscribers). Social media is key to how they share their message. 

Hillsong has relatively orthodox Protestant Christian beliefs, with a focus on the 'Kingdom of God' coming to earth as people find an enriching relationship with Jesus, rather than waiting until the afterlife. These beliefs translate into worship practices: exuberant singing to God, encounters where people 'meet God', are key parts of its Sunday church service, and inspiring the decisions they take in the rest of their lives, such as how spend their money (they are encouraged to give a 'tithe' to the church, and personal prosperity is embraced). Hillsong are involved in social action work, including via their Hillsong Citycare arm in Australia, or via sponsoring children in Uganda via charity Compassion. They run a higher education college, Hillsong College Australia, where future church leaders are trained.   

The movement has attracted controversy. Hillsong was investigated for financial irregularities by the Australian Charities and Not-for-Profits Commission, and there have been allegations of tax evasion and extravagant
spending by pastors. Founder Brian Houston was accused of concealing knowledge about child abuse, and found not guilty, but there have been other allegations of sexual harassment and abuse. Houston resigned in 2022, with USA pastor Carl Lentz fired for misconduct in 2020. These allegations had a significant negative impact on Hillsong, and many of the USA churches previously affiliated with Hillsong left Hillsong as a result. Negative reports from ex-members, for example of being expected to give a lot of money and time to volunteering for the church, circulate online. Phil and Lucinda Dooley were appointed global pastors (replacing the Houstons) in 2023. While it is hard to find membership numbers, Hillsong have an estimated global weekly attendance of 130,000.

metadata.title: Comet seeker
metadata.description:
The presented item is a refracting telescope on a tall equatorial mount tripod. The tube is made of wood, the 8 cm diameter objective and the retractable eyepiece are fixed in brass rings at opposite ends of the tube. The spotting scope is attached to the declination axis, which ends in a spherical metal counterweight on the other side. The declination axis is movably attached to the hour-angle axis.
The telescope was of compact size and offered quick disassembly, making it a convenient portable instrument. It was brought to the Astronomical Observatory in Kraków in 1834 by Józef Łęski.

metadata.title: Rushing Toward Certainty or Moving Toward Truth? Al-Ghazālī, Confirmation Bias, and Corrigible Fidelity
metadata.description:
Human beings frequently claim to seek truth when what they more urgently seek is certainty. Yet truth and certainty belong to different dimensions of epistemic life. Truth concerns whether a belief is adequate to reality; certainty concerns the confidence or security with which the belief is held. A person may therefore be certain of what is false, uncertain of what is true, or justified in holding a belief without possessing infallible assurance.

This article argues that the desire for certainty is not merely a philosophical aspiration toward secure knowledge. It is also a psychological, social, and existential force that shapes inquiry itself. It influences which evidence people seek, which authorities they trust, how they interpret disagreement, and whether they permit their worldviews to be corrected. Confirmation bias, selective exposure, motivated reasoning, and identity-protective cognition can consequently be understood as mechanisms through which the desire for certainty preserves an established worldview.

Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī's al-Munqidh min al-Ḍalāl provides the article's central point of departure. Al-Ghazālī's importance lies not merely in his methodological doubt or his historical resemblance to Descartes, but in his recognition that truth-seeking involves the moral and existential formation of the seeker. Inherited beliefs, intellectual ambition, social prestige, desire, and spiritual condition shape what a person is capable of recognizing as true. His movement from imitation through doubt toward transformative and experiential knowledge therefore expands epistemology beyond the evaluation of propositions to include the condition of the knower.

The article places al-Ghazālī in dialogue with Descartes, Peirce, James, Dewey, Wittgenstein, Popper, and virtue epistemology. Descartes represents the search for indubitable foundations; Peirce explains how doubt may be terminated without truth being attained; James and Dewey defend warranted commitment under conditions of fallibility; Wittgenstein identifies the background certainties that make inquiry possible; and Popper and virtue epistemology show why criticism requires both corrective methods and intellectual character.

The article proposes corrigible fidelity as an alternative epistemic ideal. Corrigible fidelity is the disciplined commitment to truth combined with the willingness to revise every finite formulation of it. It rejects dogmatism without collapsing into skepticism, and it permits responsible commitment without confusing conviction with infallibility. The proper aim of inquiry is therefore not the possession of final certainty, but the formation of persons, practices, and institutions capable of being corrected by truth.

metadata.title: Aspects of Integral Anthropology in Ken Wilber's Philosophy
metadata.description: Purpose. The study aims to examine the main methodological principles of Ken Wilber’s integral philosophy in the context of integral anthropology as an emerging branch of philosophical anthropology, shaped by the challenges of globalization, providing a rich toolkit for a more comprehensive understanding of human nature, consciousness, culture, and evolution. To achieve this goal, the authors aim to address the following tasks: a) explore the main aspects of integral anthropology within the framework of Ken Wilber’s philosophy; b) review potential areas of application for integral anthropology in the context of K. Wilber’s methodology. Theoretical basis. The authors of this study based their work on philosophical anthropology in both a broad and narrow sense. For them, integral anthropology as a comprehensive field of knowledge focused on the holistic study of human beings, taking into account the biological, social, cultural, psychological and spiritual aspects of their existence, is of primary importance. Originality. The work is the first to investigate the specifics of integral anthropology as a direction relevant to the contemporary era dominated by global challenges. It provides a rich set of tools for a more complete understanding of human nature, consciousness, culture, and human evolution. Using the AQAL methodology, the study explores the possibilities of practical application of the theoretical principles of integral anthropology in areas such as intercultural interaction, education, personal development, ecological anthropology, organizational transformation and leadership, the impact of spiritual practices on individuals, digital anthropology, and healthcare. Conclusions. The holistic approach of integral anthropology, grounded in Ken Wilber’s AQAL methodology, offers a comprehensive perspective on complex systems in science, society, and governance. According to Wilber, the left-hand and right-hand paths to knowledge are complementary approaches to understanding reality. The left-hand path explores the inner world and culture, while the right-hand path examines external phenomena and systems. Integral methodology in anthropology calls for considering both paths to prevent reductionism and achieve the most comprehensive understanding of the human being and their capacity to respond to contemporary global challenges.

metadata.title: SEASONAL DYNAMICS OF PHYSIOLOGICAL STATUS IN AFRICAN OSTRICHES OF VARIOUS AGE GROUPS ACCLIMATIZED TO THE CLIMATE OF UZBEKISTAN
metadata.description: This paper evaluates the seasonal fluctuations of baseline physiological markers-namely core body temperature, heart rate (HR), and respiratory rate (RR)-in African ostriches (Struthio camelus) as a function of age, sex, and lineage under the conditions of a sharply continental arid climate in Uzbekistan. The experimental cohorts comprised juvenile birds (aged 3–6 months), as well as mature 5-6-year-old males and breeding females (parent stock) representing both Iranian and Russian selection lineages. The findings indicate that the extreme heat of the summer season (“chillya”, ambient temperature exceeding +40 0C) triggers a significant compensatory response in the thermoregulatory systems of all evaluated cohorts, characterized by an elevation in body temperature and the onset of hyperventilation (polypnea). While the young stock exhibits a high metabolic rate and vegetative tone, adult birds of Iranian selection demonstrate superior evolutionary thermotolerance compared to their Russian counterparts under extreme heat loads.

metadata.title: The Little Girl & The Moon -- Accessible & Recreational Narratives
metadata.description:
This series of recreational materials was developed using resources provided by SEM Switzerland for asylum seekers, as well as some of its subcontractors such as ORS and Protectas.

It was created entirely using a basic Android phone, simple Android applications, and prompt-based interaction with widely available online AI tools, accessed via the public network.

The aim of these MP4 recreational materials, which were translated into Russian, English, French, Arabic, and German, is twofold.

 

First, to leverage the linguistic diversity present in the CFA centres.

Second, to complement existing video content that is broadcast mainly on visual terminals within these centres. 

 

At the end, we believe that, through simple drawing, writing, and the use of intelligent prompting, any asylum seeker could contribute to the creation of video or audio materials suitable for broadcast on these terminals.

To conclude, we summarise the reproducible steps as follows :

(1) We identified a visually appealing woodworking book by Bosch, in the swiss asylum center's library ;

(2) We took photographs of selected pages using a basic Android phone's camera ;

(3) We extracted images and ocerised text using native Android tools ;

(4) We used intelligent prompting to generate an allegorical and Phaedrus inspired recension of the wood assembly instructions, and translations ;

(5) We used a mainstream text-to-speech model to generate the mp3 (from ~9000 characters) ;

(6) We sketched drawn recensions of the wood assembly photographs, and took pictures to create a further diaporama ;

(7) We use the phone's native screen recorder while manually playing the mp3s and "playing" with the diaporama ;

(8) We use a mainstream phone-based video editor to reduce resolution and I terchange audio parts (whence targeted languages)

Please note that the redrawing step was not strictly necessary; however, it offers two advantages: it allows contributors to express their artistic creativity, and it helps avoid the misuse of copyrighted material by recreating the content in an original creative recension.

All the best.
